title: Heaviest Path in a Tree
statement:
You get the root of a binary tree whose values may be negative. A path is a sequence of nodes where each pair of neighbours is linked by a parent–child edge, and no node appears twice. Its weight is the sum of its values.

Return the largest weight of any path. The path must contain at least one node, and it does not have to pass through the root or end at a leaf.

Trees are written in level order with null for a missing child.

examples.why: Every value is negative, so the best path is the single largest node. An empty path with weight 0 is not allowed.
5 → 7 → 6 bends at 7 and leaves the root out. Any path that also climbs to -10 only gets lighter.
2 → 4 → 6. The left branch -5 → 3 adds -2, so the best path skips it, and it skips -1 below 4 as well.

constraints: The tree is at most 500 levels deep
hints: Every path has one highest node where it bends. If you fix that node, the path is the node plus a downward branch on each side. How heavy can each branch be?
Let gain(node) be the heaviest path that starts at node and goes only downward. A branch that weighs less than 0 is better left out, so use max(0, gain(child)).
In one post-order pass: compute l = max(0, gain(left)) and r = max(0, gain(right)), update a global best with node.val + l + r, and return node.val + max(l, r) to the parent.

explain.intuition:
Look at any path and find its highest node, where it bends. The path is that node, plus at most one downward branch into the left subtree, plus at most one into the right. To make it heavy, each branch should be the heaviest downward path from that child, unless that is negative, in which case leave the branch out. So the best path bending at X weighs X.val + max(0, gainL) + max(0, gainR). The answer is the best of that over every node.

This is the "return one thing, record another" pattern again, as for the longest walk in a tree. Each call returns the heaviest downward path from its node, which is what a parent can extend: the node plus at most one branch, because a parent cannot attach to a path that already forks. On the side, it records the heaviest bending path. The best starts at minus infinity, not 0, so a tree of all negative values still returns its largest node.
steps: Compute l = max(0, gain(node.left)) and r = max(0, gain(node.right)).
Update best = max(best, node.val + l + r): the heaviest path bending here.
pitfalls: Starting best at 0. That answers 0 for the first example, which is the weight of an empty path.
Returning node.val + l + r to the parent. A parent can only extend one branch; on [1, 5, null, 4, 6] that gives 16 instead of 15.
Forgetting to drop negative branches with max(0, …). The third example then answers 10 instead of 12.

solutions.title: Walk from every node
solutions.idea: Treat the tree as an undirected graph. From every node, walk to every other node and track the running sum. Checks every path, but costs O(n²).

solutions.title: Return the best downward gain, record the best bend
solutions.idea: One post-order pass. Each call returns the heaviest downward path from its node, and records the heaviest path that bends there.

followups: Return the nodes of the heaviest path, not just its weight.
Only paths that start at a leaf and end at a different leaf count. What changes, and what if the tree has a single leaf?
